name: Hybrid Parallel Volume Rendering
definition: A parallel programming model for raycasting volume rendering that blends message-passing (MPI) for inter-chip communication and shared-memory parallelism (pthreads or OpenMP) for intra-chip computation to improve performance, memory footprint, and communication bandwidth compared to traditional MPI-only implementations.
summary: Hybrid Parallel Volume Rendering combines MPI and threading to reduce communication costs and improve performance by multi-threading raycasting within distributed nodes.
